Orange County, CA

Blair Government Continues Criminalization of Medical Cannabis in Face of Overwhelming Public Opinion (Notice a Pattern?)
The Orange County Register, the libertarian newspaper that dominates the area between Los Angeles and San Diego, has consistently opposed prohibition in its editorials. From time to time it has taken unscientific call-in polls on the subject, which have always shown overwhelming public support for medical cannabis. On January 16, they took a poll with the question: "Do You Agree With The Decision To Charge Marvin Chavez (Orange County Cannabis Club Founder) With Selling Marijuana?" With 982 responses the vote was Yes-1% No-99%!

In the meantime, Chavez has been released on his own recognizance after two days in jail  while the DA's office says they are hunting down his volunteers. He faces eight felony counts of conspiracy and marijuana sales.

Chavez, 43, had to promise the court  not to personally purchase or distribute marijuana while awaiting trial. However, he said he will continue to be active in the co-op. His attorney, Bob Kennedy of Long Beach, said,"The club will continue to meet its obligation for those unfortunate individuals who are in need of medicinal marijuana." Just how is not clear.

"I don't know what I'm going to do," said Del Dalton, a Laguna Niguel anesthesiologist who occasionally refers patients to the co-op. "It won't do anyone any good to get a recommendation to use marijuana if they can't obtain it."

Bill Britt, 38, of Long Beach, a patient advocate for the co-op, said Chavez's arrest means the club will be forced into a less-direct role in providing pot to patients. "It will be a combination of referring other clubs, like L.A. and San Diego, and other black market sources," he said.

Last year, while I was in Los Angeles, I heard an elderly man with chronic nausea testify that -- even though he had a prescription for Marinol -- he would go to the USC campus to buy pot, because it worked better and even was cheaper than the high price prescription drug. Perhaps the Club could give out maps to the USC campus.

Meanwhile, Deputy District Attorney Carl Armbrust, who is prosecuting Chavez, said his office will respond if it hears allegations of other co-op members breaking the law."We know Chavez has some volunteers," Armbrust said. "We're trying to figure out where they are and if they're going to continue this co-op."

Chavez, 43, started the association in November 1996 after voters passed an initiative legalizing marijuana use for seriously ill people with a doctor's note, with Chavez's home serving as a makeshift headquarters.

Both sides expect the case to go to trial. "I appreciate the fact that the district attorney has given us the opportunity to let 12 jurors make the decision if it is appropriate to distribute marijuana in this manner," Kennedy said.

The co-op has suffered from the unwillingness of any Orange County community to pass an ordinance sanctioning a cannabis club or otherwise providing for the safe and affordable distribution of marijuana for medical purposes, an option permitted by the initiative. Garden Grove, home of the Crystal Cathedral, whose minister likes to talk about the value of "possibility thinking" is moving to close down its Buyers Club for considering the possibility of following Jesus' teaching. No comment from the rev.
